title: "Gallery"

Short analyses of public datasets from the
[PHPstats datasets](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets) repository, read by
URL.

**Imports** for every example on this page. The model examples also need
phit; see [Models](reference/models.qmd).

{{< include examples/gallery/_prelude.md >}}

## Subject residuals

[`sleepstudy`](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#sleepstudy) has the
average reaction time, in milliseconds, of 18 subjects on each of 10 days of
sleep deprivation (Belenky et al., 2003).

{{< include examples/gallery/_sleep.md >}}

- The common line starts at 251.4 ms on day 0 and rises 10.5 ms per day.
- Each residual is a subject's reaction time minus that line's prediction for
  the same day. Subject 337 was 77.2 ms slower than the line on average, and
  slower on all 10 days.

## Subjects as random intercepts

{{< include examples/gallery/_sleep-mixed.md >}}

- The fixed effects match the common line above: 251.4 ms on day 0 and
  10.5 ms more per day.
- The ICC is the share of the variance left after the fixed effects that
  lies between subjects.
- The intercept shifts are shrunk toward zero, so each is smaller than the
  subject's average residual above.

## Fuel economy by cylinders

[`mtcars`](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#mtcars) has fuel consumption
and design measurements for 32 cars from the 1974 *Motor Trend* magazine.
`mpg` is miles per US gallon, `hp` is gross horsepower, and `wt` is weight in
1,000 lb.

{{< include examples/gallery/_mtcars.md >}}

- `vs_group` is each car's mpg minus the mean for cars with the same number
  of cylinders.

## Labor-force participation by age

[`mroz`](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#mroz) has 753 married women in
1975 from the Panel Study of Income Dynamics: whether each was in the labor
force (`lfp`), her age, her number of children under 6 (`k5`) and from 6 to
18 (`k618`), and family income excluding her earnings (`inc`, in $1,000s).

{{< include examples/gallery/_mroz.md >}}

- `ntile()` splits the women into four groups of nearly equal size by age.
- Each odds ratio is for one more unit of its variable with the others held
  fixed: one more year of age, one more child, or $1,000 more income. One more
  child under 6 goes with odds of participation about a quarter as large. The
  ratios describe associations in these observational data.

## Warp breaks by wool and tension

[`warpbreaks`](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#warpbreaks) has the number
of warp breaks per loom for 54 looms, by wool type (A or B) and tension (low,
medium, or high).

{{< include examples/gallery/_warpbreaks.md >}}

- `asFactor()` orders tension L, M, H, so the cross-tabulation's columns
  follow it and L is the regression's reference level.
- Each rate ratio compares the expected breaks with wool A or low tension,
  holding the other factor fixed: high tension goes with 0.595 times as many
  breaks as low tension.
